tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative phrasing ('Use this skill when...', 'Apply it to classify and fix the failure'), focuses on symptoms/user-facing triggers (specific error codes, BSOD, stuck update, cluster quorum issue) rather than internal implementation, explicitly lists many trigger contexts including implicit cases ('even when the user only says one update keeps failing'), and remains a tight single paragraph.
tests.evidence: Use this skill when a Windows Server EC2 instance's update mechanism works but a specific patch fails because of the component it targets or the host's role ... even when the user only says "one update keeps failing". ... Apply it to classify and fix the failure.

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body jumps straight into component-specific diagnosis and fixes (error codes, driver conflicts, DISM commands) without explaining general concepts like what Windows Update or EC2 is. It is concise and domain-specific throughout.
tests.evidence: Driver update breaks EC2 (0x800F0217, BSOD/unreachable after a driver patch, ENA/NVMe/PV): Windows Update pushes a generic driver that overrides the AWS-specific driver

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: High-risk, fragile operations (cluster drain before reboot, driver exclusion before touching drivers) are given exact prescriptive commands, while classification and investigation steps leave room for agent judgment (e.g., 'sample signals').
tests.evidence: Suspend-ClusterNode -Drain first; rebooting an active owner or the last node loses quorum / locks CSV.

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: Each component path presents a single clear default fix (e.g., DISM RestoreHealth for .NET, driver exclusion for drivers) rather than listing multiple equal alternatives.
tests.evidence: repair with DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth + resync NGen; don't chase a standalone reinstall first.

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The skill teaches a generalizable classify-then-route-then-fix approach applicable to any instance hitting these error codes, not a one-off declaration for a specific host.
tests.evidence: Step 1: Classify the failing component (read-only) ... Step 2: Route to the component (load the matching reference)

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The skill has a dedicated Gotchas section with concrete, non-obvious corrections specific to AWS/Windows patching interactions.
tests.evidence: Windows Update drivers can break EC2 — a generic WU driver over the AWS ENA/NVMe/PV driver causes BSOD or a lost boot volume on Nitro.

tests.evidence: The skill's purpose is diagnosis and remediation, not generating a formatted report, so a template is not required.
